sections.title: History of Bioethics
sections.description: This course will take an historical approach to the emergence of modern bioethics, the study of ethical issues in medicine and the life sciences. The course will consider pre-20th century medical ethics; the scandals, tragedies and controversies that motivated the modern field; the institutionalization of bioethics in the academy, government, industry and the military; and the recent growing emphasis on ethics in basic life sciences research and development, including genetics, stem cell biology and neuroscience; and the role of bioethics in the rules-based global order. Recurring themes will include physician-patient relations, the ethics of human experimentation, military medical ethics, and human rights theory.
